title: Who Gets Flagged? The Pluralistic Evaluation Gap in AI Content Watermarking
abstract: arXiv:2604.13776v3 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: Watermarking is becoming the default mechanism for AI content authentication, with governance policies and frameworks referencing it as infrastructure for content provenance. Yet across text, image, and audio modalities, watermark signal strength, detectability, and robustness depend on statistical properties of the content itself, properties that vary systematically across languages, cultural visual traditions, and demographic groups. We examine how this content dependence creates modality-specific pathways to bias. Reviewing the major watermarking benchmarks across modalities, we find that, with one exception, none report performance across languages, cultural content types, or population groups. To address this, we propose three concrete evaluation dimensions for pluralistic watermark benchmarking: cross-lingual detection parity, culturally diverse content coverage, and demographic disaggregation of detection metrics. translated_title: 谁会被标记？AI内容水印中的多元化评估缺口
translated_abstract: 水印技术正在成为AI内容认证的默认机制，各项治理政策和框架将其作为内容溯源的基础设施。然而，在文本、图像和音频等各种模态中，水印信号的强度、可检测性和鲁棒性取决于内容本身的统计特性，而这些特性在语言、文化视觉传统和人口群体之间存在着系统性的差异。我们研究了这种内容依赖性如何产生特定于模态的偏见路径。通过回顾各模态的主要水印基准测试，我们发现除一个例外，没有任何基准测试报告了跨语言、文化内容类型或人群群体的性能表现。为解决这一问题，我们提出了多元化水印基准测试的三个具体评估维度：跨语言检测公平性、文化多样化内容覆盖以及检测指标的人口统计分解。我们认为……
tldr: 该论文揭示了AI内容水印技术因依赖内容统计特性，可能对不同语言、文化和人群产生系统性检测偏见，并提出了包含跨语言检测公平性、文化多样化内容覆盖和人口统计分组检测指标三个维度的多元化水印评估框架。
en_tdlr: This paper reveals that AI content watermarking can systematically disadvantage certain languages, cultures, and demographic groups due to its dependence on content statistical properties, and proposes a pluralistic watermarking evaluation framework with three dimensions: cross-lingual detection parity, culturally diverse content coverage, and demographic disaggregation of detection metrics.
